archetype.name: Cup Contender (possession-first)
archetype.definition: Tampa Bay controls play at 5-on-5 as well as almost anyone in the league and sits near the top of the site's rankings. It is doing so with below-par goaltending and special teams, so it looks like a top-tier team still waiting for parts of its game to catch up.

report.headline: Elite at 5-on-5; the goaltending and kill still owe them goals
report.take:
Tampa Bay is 11-4-2, fourth on the site's Teams tab, and the record is the least interesting thing about it. The Lightning own 56% of the 5-on-5 expected goals (4th) and 56% of the shot attempts (3rd). They put 29.9 shots a game on net (4th) and allow 24.5 (7th), against a league average of about 27 each way. That is a team tilting the ice most nights, and it fits the recent history: last year's 106-point side posted a .54 xGF %, and this group is pushing that higher.

The forward core carries it. Kucherov has 22 points in 17 games. Guentzel has 10 goals. Hagel ranks 5th of 126 left wings and leads the team with 65 shots. All three, plus Point and Cirelli, sit above 60% or close to it in xGF %. The blueline grades A+, with Carlson 11th among 252 defensemen and D'Astous chipping in 6 power-play points. The result is an offense ranked 6th, scoring 3.71 a game. That is not driven by hot shooting: the 12.4% all-situations shooting rate is only modestly above the league's 11.6%.

The defense ranks only 15th in goals against, and that is what the numbers hide. Tampa allows few shots, but the goalies have stopped just .882 of them (25th) and sit at -2.1 GSAx as a group. Vasilevskiy is at -0.4 and Hildeby at -1.2. This franchise's goaltending has been a plus in most recent years: +26.9 two seasons ago and +12.5 last year. The penalty kill is at 72.9% (24th) after running above 80% in each of the five prior seasons. The power play, at 19.4% (23rd), is also below its usual level. These are the leaks, and history says they are the most likely to close.

There is a modest offset. Pts vs Goal Diff is +2.2 (4th), so close games have broken their way a little, and the 5-on-5 PDO of 100.9 is a touch high. Neither is large enough to worry about. The 116-point pace will probably cool, but the underlying team looks better than a .700 points-percentage outfit with ordinary goaltending. If Vasilevskiy returns to form, this is an Atlantic favorite.

strengths.title: Owning the puck at 5-on-5
strengths.body: Tampa's 56% xGF % and 56% CF % are both top-four in the league, and it out-shoots opponents by a wide margin. The share is spread across the top nine, with Hagel, Guentzel, Point and Cirelli all above 60% in xGF %. Results built on territory rather than shooting luck are the kind that hold up.

strengths.title: Top-heavy, productive forward core
strengths.body: Kucherov drives the offense with 22 points. Guentzel and Hagel add 18 each, and Hagel's 65 shots show how much volume the top line creates. The offense is 6th in goals per game without a shooting percentage that screams regression.

strengths.title: A blueline graded A+
strengths.body: Carlson ranks 11th of 252 defensemen, and D'Astous gives the power play a second point option. Cernak and Moser post strong xGF % numbers in heavy minutes. The low shots-against total starts here.

concerns.title: Goaltending below the league line
concerns.body: An .882 team save % ranks 25th, and both goalies are under water in GSAx, so a good shot-suppression team is only middle of the pack in goals against. This is the biggest gap between process and results on the sheet. The franchise's recent goaltending history points toward recovery, but until it comes, Tampa wins on volume.

concerns.title: Special teams running cold
concerns.body: The PK at 72.9% is 24th and the PP at 19.4% is 23rd, both below league average. That is out of character: last season's kill was at 82.6%, and the power play has usually been a strength. Seventeen games of special-teams data is thin, so expect improvement, though the kill's struggles also echo the goaltending.

concerns.title: Defensemen getting loose against them
concerns.body: Opposing defensemen are out-producing their own averages against Tampa (rank 28), and their share of the points against is above the league's. Combined with the thin scoring beyond the top six, where Goncalves has no goals in 15 games of real minutes, there are cracks below the top of the lineup.

trend.note: The points percentage over the last five and ten games (.700) sits right on the season's mark. November has brought tighter defense, at 2.5 goals allowed a game after 3.31 in October, while the scoring has held.

weekAhead.headline: Three sub-.500-caliber opponents, with a back-to-back up front
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with consecutive road nights at Buffalo and Columbus, then Detroit at home. All three rank 19th or lower on the site, and all three have negative goal differentials. Tampa beat Detroit 4-2 on November 3. The back-to-back is the only real tax: expect Hildeby in one of the first two, and his -1.2 GSAx is a risk even against weak offenses.

These opponents also give Tampa's cold special teams a chance to reset. Buffalo (71.2%) and Detroit (69%) both rank near the bottom in PK %. Buffalo's power play is 30th and Columbus's 26th, which shields Tampa's leaky kill. A sweep is realistic. Five of six points is the reasonable expectation.

keyMatchups.title: Tampa's power play vs weak kills
keyMatchups.body: Buffalo's PK ranks 26th and Detroit's 28th, the softest kills Tampa will see in a while. If a 23rd-ranked power play built around Kucherov and Guentzel is going to snap out of it, this is the week.

keyMatchups.title: Columbus's goalie vs Tampa volume
keyMatchups.body: Columbus is 29th in offense and loses the shot-attempt battle. Its goalies, though, are 9th in GSAx, which makes it the opponent most likely to steal a game. Tampa's 4th-ranked shot volume should still wear on a team out-chanced at 5-on-5.

keyMatchups.title: Detroit's tight-checking structure
keyMatchups.body: Detroit allows just 23.3 shots a game (5th) and owns a strong xGF %. Its finishing is the league's worst at 9.1%, so it is an unlucky team rather than a bad one. It is also the stingiest defense Tampa sees this week, so the finale will test whether the top line can create against structure.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the team save % starts climbing toward league average. It is the one number standing between Tampa and the league's best record.

restOfSeason.body:
The 5-on-5 process is real and in line with recent seasons, so Tampa should stay a top-five team. The 116-point pace leans a little on close-game luck and should drift lower. The ptsOver figure of +2.2 and the slightly elevated 5-on-5 PDO both point that way, and they are small enough not to undo much. Two areas should pull the other way. The penalty kill and power play have both run well above their current marks in recent seasons and should recover. Goaltending is the bigger lever: an ordinary save % on this shots-against profile would make Tampa a top-five defense.

The net effect is a team that wins at roughly the same rate with a better goal differential. A finish somewhere between 104 and 114 points is the projection, enough to contend for the Atlantic with Boston and Montreal. The playoff ceiling is high if Vasilevskiy regains form and the PK gets back to normal.
swingFactors: Vasilevskiy's save % returning toward his past level
Penalty kill recovering to its historic 80%+
Depth scoring behind the top six

confidence.note: Seventeen games is small for save % and special teams, but the possession edge is large and fits recent history.
